title: IterEval: an illustrative comparison of evaluator-evolution search paths
description: Constructed illustration, not measured trajectories or an empirical comparison. IterEval names the complete framework; this panel depicts its depth-first evaluator evolution component, not preference mining. The default evaluator-evolution setup is illustrated by shallow direction switching, not a formal breadth-first-search algorithm or a universal baseline stopping rule. Each output is scored separately with a fixed base model. Numbered nodes are complete evaluation programs produced by revisions. Depth-first search continues the layout-fidelity direction. Candidate acceptance, program inheritance, and direction continuation are separate decisions; the central path illustrates eligible inheritance, not unconditional inheritance of every unsuccessful candidate. Per-pair score orderings do not establish development-cohort acceptance or generalization. Images stay fixed. The human preference and search outcomes are constructed, not collected labels or measured results.
